# Page 5^page=5
Definition of Transaction • An elementary, atomic unit of work performed by an application • Each transaction is conceptually encapsulated within two commands: • begin transaction • commit-work (commit) or rollback-work (rollback) • Transactional System (OLTP): a system that supports the execution of transactions on behalf of concurrent applications Standard SQL Commonly used

# Page 7^page=7
Bank transfer BEGIN TRANSACTION; UPDATE Account SET Balance = Balance - 10 WHERE AccNum = 42177; UPDATE Account SET Balance = Balance + 10 WHERE AccNum = 12202; COMMIT; 7

# Page 8^page=8
Event registration with limited seats BEGIN TRANSACTION; DECLARE P INTEGER; SELECT available_seats INTO P FROM Event WHERE event_id = 12 FOR UPDATE; IF P > 0 THEN UPDATE Event SET available_seats = available_seats - 1 WHERE event_id = 12; INSERT INTO Reservation(reservation_id, event_id, customer_id) VALUES (501, 12, 34); COMMIT; ELSE ROLLBACK; END IF; Remark: this example uses procedural pseudocode (variable declaration, IF). In practice, this logic may be implemented in application code or in a stored procedure FOR UPDATE temporarily locks the event row until the end of the transaction, preventing another user from performing the same operation while a user is checking and decreasing the number of available seats.

# Page 9^page=9
ACID Properties of Transactions • A transaction is a unit of work characterized by the following properties: • Atomicity • Consistency • Isolation • Durability 9

# Page 10^page=10
Atomicity • A transaction is an indivisible unit of execution • Either all the operations in the transaction are executed or none is executed • In the case of the bank transfer, the execution of a single update statement would be disastrous • The time in which COMMIT is executed marks the instant in which the transaction ends successfully: • An error before should cause the rollback of the work • An error afterwards should not alter the effect of the transaction • The ROLLBACK of the work performed can be caused • By the application with a ROLLBACK statement • By the DBMS, for example for the violation of integrity constraints or for concurrency management • In case of a rollback, the work performed must be undone, bringing the database to the state it had before the start of the transaction • It is the application’s responsibility to decide whether an aborted transaction must be redone or not 10

# Page 11^page=11
Consistency • A transaction must preserve the database integrity constraints. • Integrity constraints are normally checked at the end of each SQL statement. In such a case, each intermediate state must satisfy them. • When constraints are declared DEFERRABLE, their verification can be postponed until COMMIT. In such a case, if the initial state S0 is consistent, then the final state Sf must also be consistent. • The types of constraints that can be deferred depend on the DBMS • In PostgreSQL, UNIQUE, PRIMARY KEY, FOREIGN KEY and EXCLUDE can be deferred. CHECK and NOT NULL are checked at the end of each statement. • Integrity constraints are always checked immediately by MySQL.

# Page 12^page=12
Unique desk number CREATE TABLE Employee ( employee_id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, name VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL, desk_number INTEGER NOT NULL, CONSTRAINT unique_desk_number UNIQUE (desk_number) DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED ); id name desk 1 Alice 10 2 Bob 20 BEGIN TRANSACTION; UPDATE Employee SET desk_number = 20 WHERE employee_id = 1; UPDATE Employee SET desk_number = 10 WHERE employee_id = 2; COMMIT; -- Temporary state: desk 20 is assigned to both employees -- Final state: each desk is assigned to one employee

# Page 13^page=13
Allocated hours constraint A project has 40 planned hours. Task 1: 20 allocated hours Task 2: 20 allocated hours Constraint: sum of the allocated hours of all tasks = planned hours of the project BEGIN TRANSACTION; UPDATE Task SET allocated_hours = allocated_hours - 5 WHERE task_id = 1; UPDATE Task SET allocated_hours = allocated_hours + 5 WHERE task_id = 2; COMMIT; -- Final state: 15 + 25 = 40 constraint satisfied -- Temporary state: 15 + 20 = 35 constraint violated CREATE CONSTRAINT TRIGGER project_hours_constraint AFTER INSERT OR UPDATE OF allocated_hours ON Task DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED FOR EACH ROW …

# Page 14^page=14
Isolation • The execution of a transaction must be independent of the concurrent execution of other transactions • In particular, the concurrent execution of a number of transactions must produce the same result as the execution of the same transactions in a sequence • E.g., the concurrent execution of transactions T1 and T2 must produce the same results that can be obtained by executing one of these sequences • T1,T2 • T2,T1 • Isolation impacts performance and trade-offs can be defined between isolation and performance

# Page 15^page=15
Durability • The effect of a transaction that has successfully committed will last "forever" • Independently of any system fault • Sounds obvious… but every DBMS manipulates data in main memory

# Page 16^page=16
ACID properties & DBMS mechanisms • Atomicity • Abort-rollback-restart, commit protocols • Reliability Manager • Consistency • Integrity checking of the DBMS • Integrity Control System at query execution time (with the support of the DDL compiler) • Isolation • Concurrency control • Concurrency Control System • Durability • Recovery management • Reliability Manager
